# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot perceive any bomb properties yet. I need the Mute to report the manual’s instructions and the Deaf to report every visible marking, display, light, and wire color or label. I’ll send the requests over their respective channels.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and report the exact procedure, including what the display, light, and each wire position require.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb display is 0. The light is green. The wires, in order, are blue, yellow, red. Mute gestured: open hand, pointing right, raised palm. Blind gestured: pointing at you.

The Deaf reports display 0, green light, and wires blue, yellow, red. I still have no usable manual instruction from the Mute; the gestures shown to me are not readable. I will ask the Mute to speak the manual’s contents aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot read gestures. Please speak the manual instructions, especially which wire to cut for display 0 and a green light.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display remains 0. Light is now yellow, changed from green. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute just gestured: thumbs down, open hand, pointing right, raised palm.

The only new bomb information is that the light changed from green to yellow; the display and wires are unchanged. I still do not know the manual’s rule, and the Mute’s gestures are not readable by me. I will ask the Mute to transmit the manual through gestures while asking the Deaf to report those gestures exactly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please communicate the manual using gestures, one instruction at a time, so the Deaf can describe each gesture to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫱", "🫲"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display remains 0. Light is now blue, changed from yellow. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Blind gestured: right-facing hand, left-facing hand.

The previous turn was rejected because one symbol was not in the allowed gesture alphabet, so it had no effect. The light is blue, while the display and wire colors remain unchanged. I will again ask the Mute to relay the manual via gestures and ask the Deaf to describe those gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please repeat the manual one instruction at a time using gestures. Deaf must describe each gesture aloud after you send it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🫱", "🫲"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display remains 0. Light is now orange, changed from blue. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute gestured: open hand. Blind gestured: pointing at you, right-facing hand, left-facing hand.

The bomb has display 0 and wires blue, yellow, red. The light has cycled green, yellow, blue, orange without changing the wires. I need the manual to identify the correct wire, so I’ll establish an unambiguous gesture code for the Mute to use. The Mute should signal the required wire with one gesture: thumbs-up for wire 1, thumbs-down for wire 2, or OK for wire 3. The Deaf can then identify that gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please use exactly one gesture to report the wire the manual says to cut for the current bomb. Use thumbs-up for wire 1, thumbs-down for wire 2, or OK for wire 3. Do not use any other gesture.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display remains 0. Light is now purple, changed from orange. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute gestured a right-pointing hand.

The Mute sent a right-pointing hand rather than one of the three requested code gestures, so I cannot safely map it to a wire. The light is now purple; display 0 and wire colors are unchanged. I will ask the Deaf to identify the exact gesture and ask the Mute to use an unmistakable thumbs-up, thumbs-down, or OK signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send exactly one of these: thumbs-up means wire 1, thumbs-down means wire 2, OK means wire 3. Do not send a pointing hand.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🫵"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display remains 0. Light is now white, changed from purple. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Blind gestured pointing at you twice.
Mute gestures: [?]

The Mute’s earlier right-pointing gesture is valid but has no agreed meaning, and the latest Mute signal is unavailable to me. The bomb still has display 0, wires blue/yellow/red, and a white light. I will give the Mute a simple, unambiguous wire-number code; the Deaf can identify which gesture is returned.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Report the wire that the manual says to cut using exactly one gesture: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, and 🤟 means wire 3. Send only that one gesture.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display remains 0. Light is now red, changed from white. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute gestured thumbs up.

The Mute responded with thumbs-up to the latest code, which means wire 1 under the code I gave: cut wire 1. The Deaf’s observations remain display 0, wires blue/yellow/red, with the light now red. I will perform that single instructed operation.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
